corpus_definition: different from what is usual, expected, or typical

forms.definition: something that is not usual, often in the body
forms.example: The doctor found no abnormality in the X-ray.

forms.definition: different from what is usual, often in a worrying way
forms.example: This hot weather is abnormal for March.

syn.note: Not happening in the usual pattern.

forms.definition: in a way that is not usual
forms.example: It was abnormally cold in April.

context.text: The doctor said Akmal's high temperature was abnormal. It stayed abnormally high for three days.

reviewer_note: normal is the opposite, so it sits in ant.

corpus_definition: the state of not being present somewhere

forms.definition: the fact of not being in a place where you should be
forms.example: Her absence from class worried the teacher.

syn.note: Formal: not going to school or work.

ant.note: Being present at school or work.

forms.definition: not in the place where you are expected to be
forms.example: Three students are absent today.

syn.note: Not where it should be, and nobody knows where.

forms.definition: in a way that shows you are thinking about something else
forms.example: He nodded absently.
forms.note: Belongs to absent = not paying attention, not being away.

people.definition: a person who is not at school or work when expected
people.example: There were five absentees at the meeting.

context.text: Bekzod was absent from school on Monday. His teacher asked his mother about the reason for his absence.

reviewer_note: absently is a different sense. verb "absent yourself" is formal and rare, so no_form.

corpus_definition: A way of speaking typical of a certain region.

forms.definition: the way people from one place or country say words
forms.example: She speaks English with a Russian accent.

syn.note: A local form of a language, with its own words too.

forms.definition: to make something easier to notice
forms.example: The dress accentuates her eyes.
forms.note: Belongs to accent = special attention to something, not a way of speaking.

forms.definition: spoken with the accent of another place
forms.example: He speaks heavily accented English.

context.text: My cousin from Khorezm has a strong local accent. Even his accented Russian sounds friendly and warm.

reviewer_note: Two corpus rows (B2, B1) merged; B1 used. Accent on a letter or word is a different sense, not covered.

corpus_definition: the right or ability to enter or use something

forms.definition: the right or chance to enter a place or use something
forms.example: Students have free access to the library.

syn.note: The right to go into a place.
Permission to enter, often with a ticket.

forms.definition: how easy something is to reach, enter or use
forms.example: The new metro improved accessibility for wheelchair users.

forms.definition: to enter a place or get information, often on a computer
forms.example: You can access your results online.

forms.definition: easy to reach, enter or use
forms.example: The museum is accessible by bus.

ant.note: Impossible or very hard to reach.

context.text: Our new school building has a ramp, so it is accessible for everyone. All pupils also get free internet access in the library.

corpus_definition: A place to stay like a hotel room.

forms.definition: a place where you live or stay, like a room or flat
forms.example: The price includes flights and accommodation.
forms.note: Uncountable in British English; American English often uses "accommodations".

syn.note: A place to stay, more formal or old-fashioned.
Houses and flats for people to live in.

forms.definition: to give someone a place to stay, or to have room for
forms.example: The hotel can accommodate two hundred guests.

syn.note: Give people a place to live.

forms.definition: happy to help and do what people want
forms.example: The staff were very accommodating.
forms.note: Belongs to accommodate = help, not giving a room.

context.text: Finding accommodation in Samarkand is easy in winter. In spring, small hotels can only accommodate a few guests, so book early.

reviewer_note: accommodating = helpful is a different sense.

forms.definition: the quality of being correct and exact
forms.example: Check the accuracy of your answers.

ant.note: A mistake, or not being exact.

forms.definition: correct and exact, with no mistakes
forms.example: The weather report was accurate.

forms.definition: in a correct and exact way
forms.example: Measure the room accurately.

context.text: The new map app is very accurate. It shows accurately where every bus is in Tashkent.

corpus_definition: A dull, continuous feeling of being hurt in your body.

forms.definition: a pain that is not strong but goes on for a long time
forms.example: I have an ache in my back.

syn.note: General word; can be sudden or strong.
Pain from tired or hurt muscles.

forms.definition: to feel a dull pain that goes on and on
forms.example: My legs ached after the long walk.

forms.definition: feeling a dull, long pain
forms.example: He rubbed his aching shoulders.

context.text: After a day in the cotton fields, Grandpa feels an ache in his back. He sits down and rests his aching legs.

reviewer_note: headache, toothache are compounds, left out (rule 7).

corpus_definition: to calculate the total amount of several numbers
particle_note: Separable: "add up the numbers / add the numbers up"; with a pronoun only "add them up". "add up to" = make a total: "It adds up to 50,000 som."

context.text: At the bazaar Ulugbek added up the prices in his head. The fruit and bread added up to 45,000 som.

reviewer_note: "It doesn't add up" (makes no sense) not covered.

corpus_definition: an event, situation, or matter that needs attention

forms.definition: an event or situation, or a matter people must deal with
forms.example: The wedding was a big family affair.
forms.note: Plural affairs = public or personal business: "current affairs". "an affair" can also mean a secret love relationship.

syn.note: A subject or situation to deal with.
Something that is your concern: "It is my business."
Something that happens, like a party.

context.text: The opening of the new park was a big affair in our town. The mayor said the park is now an affair for all citizens.

corpus_definition: To cause a change in someone or something.

forms.definition: a feeling of liking and love for someone
forms.example: She has great affection for her grandmother.
forms.note: Belongs to an old sense of affect = feelings, not causing change.

forms.definition: to change or influence someone or something
forms.example: Cold weather affects the cotton harvest.
forms.note: affect is a verb; effect is the noun (the result).

syn.note: Have an effect on how something develops.
Have a strong effect; more formal.

forms.definition: changed or harmed by something
forms.example: People in affected areas need help.

context.text: The long summer heat affected many farms. Families in the affected villages got water from the government.

reviewer_note: Two corpus rows (B2, B1) merged; B1 used. effect is a different word, listed as not_family.

gate_overrides.reason: affection is a suffix derivation (affect + -ion), not a compound; it is shown as other_meaning (Oxford/Cambridge learner noun).
